text.p: Commodore Environmental Services said Monday it obtained control of Lanxide Corp for an undisclosed sum.
Lanxide said it agreed to sell up to $25 million of preferred stock to Commodore, which would give Commodore control over the company.
Lanxide said the deal calls for Commodore to initially invest $2 million in preferred stock and another $8.5 million by August 27, of which $4.5 million represents canceled debt.

Commodore also received a warrant to buy up to $14.5 million of preferred stock by July 3 2000, Lanxide said, adding Commodore can convert the preferred stock into the company's common stock at $7.41 a share.

Lanxide posted a loss of $2.70 a share on $4.0 million in revenues in the first quarter, compared with a profit of $0.10 a share on sales of $5.5 million the year before. Its stock closed at 10 June 30.

The company's chief executive Marc Newkirk said in a statement the influx of resources from Commodore coupled with the large market for Lanxide's products should lead to "accelerated growth for years to come."
Commodore said Monday today's deal ends the merger discussions between the companies, which started in November last year.

The company's chief executive, Paul Hannesson, said in a statement "the transformation of Commodore into a material sciences company should prove beneficial to the stockholders of both Commodore and Lanxide."

Commodore posted a loss of $0.04 a share on revenues of $5.0 million in the first quarter, compared with a loss of $0.02 a share on revenues of $111,000 the year before.Its stock closed at 3/4 July 2, close to its 52-week low of 5/8.
The company, which holds 69.3 percent of Commodore Applied Technologies Inc, said Lanxide is the second publicly-traded company in which it owns a majority stake.
